title: A small dense set of representable hypercovers
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category with a Grothendieck topology $J$ given by covering sieves: a sieve is a set of arrows into an object closed under precomposition, the maximal sieve covers, and covering sieves satisfy pullback stability and transitivity. No fibre products or subcanonicity are assumed. Use [def-weil-size-convention] for universes and [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] for associated sheaves.

Write $h_T(V)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(V,T)$. A hypercover $U_\bullet\to h_T$ is an augmented simplicial presheaf of sets whose terms are small coproducts of representables and whose augmented matching maps become epimorphisms after sheafification. The degree-zero matching presheaf is $h_T$; all higher matching presheaves, parametrizing compatible proper faces, are formed in presheaves. A refinement over $T$ means a morphism of augmented simplicial presheaves over $h_T$. A collection is dense if every hypercover over every $T$ admits a refinement by a member of that collection over the same $T$.

There is a small set $\mathcal H_0$ of hypercovers with varying targets which is dense. More precisely there is an uncountable regular cardinal $\kappa$, in the working universe and larger than the cardinality of the arrows of $\mathcal C$, such that every hypercover admits a refinement whose total number of representable summands in all degrees is less than $\kappa$. A set of representatives up to isomorphism of the hypercovers satisfying this bound can be chosen as $\mathcal H_0$.

source.place: Dugger--Hollander--Isaksen, Hypercovers and simplicial presheaves, arXiv:math/0205027v2, Definition 6.1 and Proposition 6.6 with its proof, pp. 16, 18-19 (published numbering: Proposition 6.7); Choudhury--Gallauer, Fact 5.2.
